problem_statement: When coap_build_reply() is asked to build a reply with code 0, the result must be a RST message with no token: the generated packet must have type RST, code 0, and token length 0, and no request token bytes may be copied into the reply, even when the request has a token. The fmt module must also provide a function that converts a hexadecimal string to a byte array; it accepts each pair of hexadecimal digits as one output byte, accepts both upper- and lower-case hex digits, returns the number of bytes written, returns -EINVAL when the input length is odd or the string contains a non-hex character, and returns -EOVERFLOW when the decoded result would not fit in the destination buffer.

problem_statement_fixed: When coap_build_reply() is asked to build a reply with code 0, the result must be a RST message with no token: the generated packet must have type RST, code 0, and token length 0, and no request token bytes may be copied into the reply, even when the request has a token. The generated packet must not modify any bytes beyond the generated packet. The fmt module must also provide a function, named scn_buf_hex and declared in fmt.h with the signature ssize_t scn_buf_hex(void *dest, size_t dest_len, const char *hex, size_t hex_len), that converts a hexadecimal string to a byte array; it accepts each pair of hexadecimal digits as one output byte, accepts both upper- and lower-case hex digits, returns the number of bytes written, returns -EINVAL when the input length is odd or the string contains a non-hex character, and returns -EOVERFLOW when the decoded result would not fit in the destination buffer. It must not modify any bytes in the destination beyond the number of bytes written.
